name: 100ads.ai
tagline: Generates large batches of ad copy and creative variations from a product description or landing page.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Bulk ad variation generation is one of the most one-shottable AI products there is: scrape a landing page, build a structured prompt, loop it a hundred times, dedupe, export. An agent can get you headline and primary text variants in Meta and Google character limits in an evening, plus image variants if you wire up an image model. The gaps are everything after generation: pushing creatives into live ad accounts, pulling performance data back, and learning which angles actually convert. If the product's real pitch is a performance feedback loop across many advertisers, your local clone is just a very fast copywriter with no scoreboard. If the pitch is volume, you already won.
coreLoopDIY: Takes a product URL or description, generates dozens of ad copy variants per angle within platform character limits, and exports them as CSV ready for bulk upload.
requirements: An OpenAI or Anthropic API key
An image model API key if you want creative, not just copy
Patience for reading 100 ad variants and throwing out 90
whatYouLose: No direct push into Meta or Google Ads, you upload CSVs by hand
No performance data flowing back, so nothing ranks your variants except your own taste
No cross-account benchmarks on which angles work in your vertical
No brand voice memory or asset library unless you build the storage yourself
Image generation quality and ad-safe text rendering stay a genuine pain
moatNotes: The only durable asset here is aggregate creative performance data across advertisers. Generation itself is a commodity wrapped around someone else's model.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the annoying part of running ads is not writing a hundred headlines, it is getting them into ad accounts in the right formats with the right naming conventions and then knowing which ones to kill. Tools like this sell the whole lane, not the generation step. People also pay to skip the prompt engineering and the per-platform character limit bookkeeping, which is unglamorous and easy to get subtly wrong.
notes: Generation is free, distribution and measurement are not. Your clone writes ads; it does not tell you which ones work.
prompt:
Build a local ad variation generator called adforge. Stack: Node 20, TypeScript, Next.js App Router, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3. No auth, no cloud, no telemetry. Single user, runs on localhost.

Core flow:
1. A form takes either a product URL or a pasted description, plus audience, tone, and offer fields.
2. If a URL is given, fetch it server side and extract title, meta description, headings, and the first 2000 characters of body text with cheerio. Show the extraction so the user can edit it before generating.
3. Define a fixed list of marketing angles in code: pain point, outcome, social proof, curiosity, objection handling, urgency, comparison, founder story.
4. For each angle, call the Anthropic Messages API and request structured JSON with N copy variants. Each variant has: headline, primary text, description, call to action, angle, and a one-line rationale.
5. Enforce platform constraints server side after generation: Meta headline 40 chars, primary text 125 chars recommended, description 30 chars; Google RSA headline 30 chars, description 90 chars. Flag anything over limit instead of silently truncating.
6. Store every generation run and variant in SQLite. Dedupe near-identical variants with a simple normalized-string hash.

UI: one page to create a run, one page per run showing variants in a sortable table grouped by angle, with inline edit, a keep/kill toggle, and character counters that turn red past the limit.

Export: download kept variants as a Meta bulk-import CSV and as a Google Ads RSA CSV, with correct column headers for each.

Explicitly out of scope: image generation, Meta or Google OAuth, pushing live ads, performance tracking, team accounts, billing. Do not stub these in the UI.

Secrets: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local, read server side only. Ship a .env.example.

Deliver: working npm run dev, a seed script with one example run so the UI is not empty, and a README with setup in under ten lines.
